title: Housing menu UI: NPC banners, query, assign and evict
player_outcome: A Housing tab in the inventory lists every resident's head banner. Press '?' and click a room to hear 'This housing is suitable.' or what is missing. Click a banner, then a room, to move that NPC in; right-click a banner to evict them. While the tab is open, banners hang in each occupied room.
design: New game/UI/HousingPanel.cs, a Control added as a tab of the equipment column through a new InventoryScreen.Tabs.cs partial (AddTab(name, icon, control)), to limit conflicts with the UI phase's inventory layout. It holds a grid of portrait buttons (PortraitIcons) for residents that are CountsAsResident or pets: tooltip 'Name the X — lives at … / homeless', a greyed look when dead or homeless, and a '?' query button.

World picking with the mouse free: a new game/UI/WorldPicker.cs. Camera.ProjectRayOrigin/Normal from the mouse position → Core Targeting.Cast(world, origin, dir, 40 m) → the air cell (hit.Cell + hit.Normal).

Modes: query (next left click → Game.Town.QueryHousing(cell) → Message to ChatLog or Hud.Announce in Terraria yellow Color8(255,240,20), with the room outline flashed using SelectionMesh or TargetHighlight's box for 1.5 s); assign (click a banner, the cursor shows the head, click a room → AssignHome → message); evict (right-click a banner → Evict).

New game/Entities/HousingBannerRenderer.cs: while the Housing tab is open, a pooled Sprite3D per housed resident shows the head texture at BannerCell (billboard off, hanging on a small cloth quad). The nodes are hidden when the tab closes and allocated once.
Engine commands 'ui housing' (open the tab) and 'ui housing_query dx dy dz'; probe ui.housing_open.
tests: Core coverage is in P5-05; UI smoke in town.cmds: 'ui inventory' / 'ui housing' / 'assert ui.housing_open == 1' / 'ui housing_query 8 1 0' / 'ui close' / 'assert errors == 0'
verification: In game: the query shows the missing-requirement message; drag the Merchant into the Guide's house → they swap; banners visible only while the tab is open; F3 shows no frame spike when toggling
risks: The UI phase re-anchors InventoryScreen (Terraria layout with equipment column tabs); coordinate the tab strip placement. This package only adds the partial and one call.
Inventory-open input gating (audit L) must still allow clicking the world while the Housing tab is open; the picker handles clicks itself.
